newsitem.title: GREECE: Greece welcomes Holbrooke as Cyprus envoy.
newsitem.headline: Greece welcomes Holbrooke as Cyprus envoy.

text.p: Greece on Thursday welcomed Bosnian peacemaker Richard Holbrooke's appointment as President Clinton's special emissary for the divided island of Cyprus, saying it signalled renewed U.S. interest.
"The Holbrooke appointment is a clear indication of the strong interest by the United States to take an initiative to resolve the Cyprus problem," government spokesman Dimitris Reppas told reporters.
But he was quick to point out that Greece would not accept any intervention from the envoy in Greek-Turkish disputes over rights in the Aegean Sea.

"The Cyprus issue and the matter of Greek-Turkish relations are separate," Reppas said. "Mr. Holbrooke is President Clinton's envoy for the Cyprus issue. His initiative has nothing to do with Greek-Turkish issues or Aegean issues."
Holbrooke, out of government service for more than a year, was named on Wednesday and will replace Richard Beattie, amid fresh efforts to reunite the island in a federation.

Cyprus has been divided since Turkish troops occupied its northern third in 1974 after a short-lived coup in Nicosia, backed by the military junta then ruling Greece. A self-declared Turkish-Cypriot state in the north is recognised only by Turkey.
President Glafkos Clerides of Cyprus and Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash are due to meet on July 9 in New York for U.N.-sponsored talks.
Holbrooke, who made a name for himself as the tough negotiator who pulled off the Balkan peace agreement in Dayton, Ohio, in November 1995, played down prospects of a rapid success in Cyprus.
"I don't want to leave you with the idea that we have the magic bullet," he told Reuters.
